question: What does fluid dynamics study in the human body?

options.A: How fluids move and behave within the body
options.B: The chemical composition of human blood
options.C: How solid organs absorb nutrients from food
options.D: The electrical signals generated by the heart

explanation: Fluid dynamics looks at how liquids and gases flow, which helps us understand how blood circulates and IV fluids move. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T4#BMP112_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why is knowing how fluids move important for a midwife?

options.A: It is the primary method used to calculate fetal gestational age
options.B: It guides the nutritional composition of antenatal dietary plans
options.C: It allows midwives to perform surgical repairs of blood vessels
options.D: It helps in managing intravenous lines and understanding circulation

explanation: Understanding fluid flow helps midwives safely give IV treatments and keep track of a mother's heart and blood health. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T4#BMP112_U3_T4_h1)

question: What does the word 'viscosity' mean for a liquid?

options.A: Its total volume within a closed container
options.B: Its temperature relative to the body
options.C: Its thickness and resistance to flowing
options.D: The speed at which it evaporates in heat

explanation: Viscosity is simply how thick a fluid is and how much it resists flowing. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T4#BMP112_U3_T4_h2)

question: How does severe anemia affect the thickness or viscosity of a patient's blood?

options.A: It stops viscosity completely by halting all cellular movement
options.B: It has no effect on viscosity because only water content matters
options.C: It increases viscosity due to an overproduction of plasma proteins
options.D: It decreases viscosity because red blood cell numbers are reduced

explanation: Red blood cells make blood thick, so having fewer cells means lower viscosity and thinner blood. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T4#BMP112_U3_T4_h2)

question: Which flow pattern describes fluid moving in smooth, parallel layers?
explanation: Laminar flow is smooth and orderly, where the center moves fastest and the edges move slowest along the sides. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T4#BMP112_U3_T4_h3)

question: What usually causes turbulent, swirling flow inside a blood vessel?

options.A: A sudden narrowing or rough patch inside a blood vessel
options.B: A smooth, wide artery with very slow-moving blood
options.C: An evenly dilated vein carrying plasma without red cells
options.D: Normal resting circulation through healthy capillary beds

explanation: Narrow spots or rough patches break up smooth layers, turning the flow into a chaotic swirl. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T4#BMP112_U3_T4_h3)

question: According to Poiseuille's law, which factor has the biggest impact on how fast fluid flows through a tube?

options.A: The room temperature of the ward
options.B: The total length of the tube
options.C: The color of the intravenous bag

explanation: Because the radius has a massive mathematical effect in the formula, even a tiny change in tube width greatly alters the flow speed. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T4#BMP112_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why would a midwife choose a wider cannula instead of a longer one when fluids need to be given quickly?

options.A: Wider cannulas prevent the blood cells from sticking together inside the plastic tubing
options.B: Longer tubes increase fluid viscosity while wider tubes cool the liquid down instantly
options.C: A wider radius increases fluid flow rate, whereas increased length slows it down
options.D: Pressure gradients only work when the IV tubing is kept as short as physically possible

explanation: Making the cannula wider increases the flow speed, while making it longer adds resistance and slows the fluid down. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T4#BMP112_U3_T4_h4)

question: What happens to the flow rate of a gravity IV when you hang the fluid bag higher?

options.A: The flow rate increases because the pressure gradient becomes greater
options.B: The flow rate decreases because gravity pulls the liquid backward
options.C: The flow rate stays exactly the same regardless of bag height
options.D: The fluid viscosity doubles instantly inside the hanging plastic bag

explanation: Raising the bag increases the pressure driving the fluid down, making it flow faster. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T4#BMP112_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why is a wide-gauge cannula used instead of a tiny needle when giving a blood transfusion to a postpartum patient?

options.A: Blood products have low viscosity and will leak out of small needles too quickly
options.B: Tiny needles cause blood to freeze solid inside the plastic tubing during infusion
options.C: Thicker blood needs a wider bore to prevent slow flow and cellular damage from high resistance
options.D: Wide gauges are only required to prevent the IV site from swelling with saline

explanation: Blood is thicker than saline, so it needs a wider needle to flow smoothly without high resistance. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T4#BMP112_U3_T4_h5)

question: How does blood composition normally change during a healthy pregnancy?

options.A: An extreme increase in red blood cell production that doubles viscosity
options.B: Severe hemoconcentration, where plasma drops and blood becomes thick as honey
options.C: Total loss of all plasma proteins, stopping normal clotting mechanisms
options.D: Hemodilution, where plasma increases more than red cells, lowering viscosity

explanation: Pregnancy naturally adds more liquid plasma than red cells, which thins out the blood to help support the baby. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T4#BMP112_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why does severe dehydration increase the risk of blood clots in postpartum women?

options.A: Lack of body water stops the liver from producing any blood-thinning enzymes
options.B: Dehydration lowers blood pressure so much that circulation stops entirely
options.C: Thickened, highly viscous blood flows sluggishly through vessels, encouraging stasis and clot formation
options.D: Dehydration causes all red blood cells to dissolve completely into clear serum

explanation: When blood loses water and gets too thick, it moves slowly through the vessels, making it easier for clots to form. [learn more](BMP112_U3_T4#BMP112_U3_T4_h6)
